caveats: Logical NTRN transfers, physical BOCs and RPCs use different units.
Canonical TPS counts proof-checked block gen_utime buckets; offered/admitted TPS use the 600s issuance phase.
A comparison needs repeated gain before promotion; capacity needs at least 5% actual offered headroom and capacity validity.
All-arm RTT percentiles include warmup and drain unless a measured histogram is explicitly present.
CPU sample means are not integrated CPU work. External host activity and evolving chain/cache state remain confounders.

comparison.attribution: validator image transition with the same client; includes rebuild/compiler/layout effects, not feature isolation

interpretation: Successful bundled prerequisite callbacks only; no failed/timed-out/cancelled callback population.
Samples are requests made by shard collators, not accepted or canonical blocks. Repeated MC block IDs remain separate requests.
Queue intervals measure enqueue/callback scheduling wall delays; asynchronous waits also include downstream service, scheduling and possible I/O.
Local service intervals are wall time, not CPU time, and can include preemption.
Per-request groups sum non-overlapping logged intervals. Percentiles are calculated from each request sum, never by summing interval percentiles.
Summed request wall times overlap between concurrent collators and are not elapsed benchmark duration, CPU usage or TPS.
Fraction denominators are summed request wall time across samples. Do not add these timings to enclosing collation/perf timers.
The profile covers the bundled candidate path only; it cannot by itself establish a reduction relative to the legacy path.
Window selection uses callback-log timestamps in [start,end); a selected request may have begun before start.
Multiple source logs are concatenated without deduplication. Supply disjoint captures to avoid double-counting.
Counts are completed full-candidate encode log events, not canonical blocks, accepted transactions, logical transfers, network sends, or TPS.
Empty candidates and cache hits have no serialize_candidate log. There is no explicit cache-hit/miss counter.
Root multiplicity groups a block root, not an immutable Candidate object, slot or consensus session. Distinct envelopes/lifetimes may share the root.
Single-validator normal generation uses one consensus overlay encode and one durable store encode on the same object. Request/reload paths can add encodes.

The compressed timer begins after original block and collated-data BOC decoding. It covers combined-root serialization and LZ4 work, but excludes initial decode, outer envelope/copies and cache synchronization.
Uncompressed timer semantics differ: it covers serialization of the validatorSession candidate object; compression mode is reported separately.
Durations are wall time, not CPU. Concurrent encode durations overlap; their sum is not benchmark elapsed time or a throughput rate.
Byte totals count encoder input/output repeatedly; they exclude outer envelopes and do not measure bytes sent on the network.
Selection uses UTC callback-log timestamps in [start,end). An encode can begin before start, and encodes for the same root may straddle either boundary.
A root with one event does not prove cache reuse: the other encode may be outside the window, omitted from logs, cancelled, or belong to an unobserved actor.
Multiple distinct log files are concatenated without line deduplication; use disjoint captures from the intended validator process only.
Candidate payload caching does not directly change collator create_block_candidate timing or separate full-node broadcast formats.

join: Match consensus.stats.blockAccepted to consensus.stats.candidateReceived by (enclosing session ID, candidate slot, candidate hash).
Extract candidateReceived.block.id only for consensus.stats.block full candidates.
Join to validatorStats.collatedBlock by exact (workchain, shard, seqno, root_hash, file_hash).
Select workchain 0 blocks by earliest local acceptance event in exact decimal [start,end).
Deduplicate repeated acceptance events by candidate ID and full block identity; exclude ambiguous duplicate collation records.
interpretation: Local manager acceptance is not independently proven canonical masterchain anchoring. Do not call this population canonical-only or derive canonical TPS from it.
Metrics attached to an accepted block cover its full collation; some selected blocks were collated before the window boundary.
total_time is the full observed collation wall envelope, including asynchronous prerequisites and external waits; it is not active CPU service.
work_time and cpu_work_time are scoped, incompletely encompassing collation counters. Native fast-path stages have separate scopes; do not infer missing idle time by subtraction.
wait_externals_time is the sum of timed external-queue probes/refill/first-work waits and callback scheduling. It is distinct from masterchain prerequisite round trips.
native_commit includes account materialization, dictionary updates, proof checkpoint rebuild and size preflight. Do not add parent and child times.
create_state_merkle_update is included in create_shard_state. Stages can overlap with enclosing timers and concurrent blocks.

native_stat_checkpoint_rebuild covers the trial limit/stat setup, immutable-base snapshot/copy or overlay setup, and evolving account-root proof traversal. It excludes the separately timed hard/size preflight.
create_block_candidate serializes initial block/proof BOCs and performs size checks before consensus Candidate creation. It does not measure Candidate::serialize cache work.
External delivery producer_pending is sampled at wait entry. False does not prove that clients offered no useful work for the whole interval.
The diagnostic changes runtime verbosity near its end; both windows are diagnostic-only, not an A/B throughput comparison.
